STAGE 1 of a 4-stage pipeline on /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui.

YOUR JOB: independently VALIDATE OR DISPROVE four claims by EXECUTION, not by reading. You are the proof stage — a later agent will implement fixes only for claims you confirm. Do NOT fix anything. Do NOT commit. READ-ONLY except for temporary probe files you delete afterwards (verify `git status` is clean before you finish).

Allowed: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`, `npx tsx -e`, `npx eslint`, `node`, git read commands, temporary probe files under overrides/ that you delete.
FORBIDDEN: `npm start`, `npm run build-storybook`, `npx test-storybook` (another process owns those and a concurrent build collides). Do not modify any tracked file.

=== CLAIM M1 ===
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx:140-143` has two `as` casts justified by this comment: "TypeScript cannot index a discriminated union type directly — each branch must be cast individually to access the relevant key without a type error."
Claim: the comment is FACTUALLY FALSE — the casts are unnecessary and the file compiles clean without them. Additional claim: the casts silently widen `'aria-hidden': true` to `boolean` and erase the XOR guarantee of `ZimmIconProps`.
PROVE by: copying the file, deleting both casts, compiling under the project tsconfig. Then separately prove or disprove the widening/XOR claim — construct a probe that would be REJECTED with the XOR intact and check whether it is accepted with the casts present.

=== CLAIM M2 ===
`overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx:181-182`:
  const footer = canvasElement.querySelector('footer[role="contentinfo"]') as HTMLElement;
  const slot = footer.querySelector('[aria-live]') as HTMLElement;
Claim: both casts are unjustified (no comment, which typescript.md requires), the real work they do is asserting non-null (which typescript.md treats like `!`), and the `HTMLElement` widening buys nothing because `Element` already has `getBoundingClientRect`.
PROVE by: compiling variants — (a) casts removed entirely, (b) `querySelector<HTMLElement>(...)` with a null guard, (c) as-is. Report which compile and what each changes. State what happens at RUNTIME if the selector misses, under each variant.

=== CLAIM S6 ===
`overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` lines ~104, ~125, ~126: `links: FooterNavLinkEntry[]`, `navGroups: FooterNavGroupEntry[]`, `legalLinks?: FooterNavLinkEntry[]` should be `readonly`/`ReadonlyArray` per typescript.md, because the footer only maps over them and `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is a module-level singleton any consumer could mutate.
PROVE by: (1) confirming the footer only reads them — find every use; (2) writing a probe that MUTATES `FOOTER_FIXTURE.fields.navGroups` and confirming it currently compiles (demonstrating the exposure is real); (3) applying `readonly` in a copy and confirming the probe is then rejected AND the rest of the codebase still compiles. That last part is the important one — if `readonly` breaks existing code, say so.

=== CLAIM S7 ===
`overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx:2` imports `Meta`/`StoryObj` from `@storybook/react`, which is claimed NOT to be a declared dependency (only a transitive child of `@storybook/react-webpack5`), while 11 other stories use `@storybook/react-webpack5`.
PROVE by: checking package.json, `npm ls`, and whether the two modules export structurally compatible `Meta`/`StoryObj`. Confirm switching the import compiles. Note whether this is purely type-level.

FOR EACH CLAIM output: **CONFIRMED** / **DISPROVED** / **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED**, the exact command(s) and their output as evidence, and — if confirmed — the minimal correct fix with the reason it is minimal. If a claim is overstated in any part, say precisely which part. A disproved claim is a valuable result; do not manufacture confirmation.

End with `git status --porcelain` output proving you left the tree clean.

export type ZimmIconType =
  | 'arrow-down'
  | 'arrow-link'

  | 'profile'
  | 'search'
  | 'share'
  | 'share-2'
  | 'wishlist'
  | 'wishlist-selected'
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  | 'phone'
  | 'whatsapp'
  | 'email';

export type ZimmIconSize = keyof typeof iconSizes;

type ZimmIconProps = {
  type: ZimmIconType;
  size?: ZimmIconSize;
  /** Pass Chakra token strings or CSS keywords (e.g. 'text.primary', 'currentColor').
   *  Do not pass hardcoded hex values — use theme tokens. */
  color?: string;
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: FavouritesIcon,
  'wishlist-selected': FavouritesSolidIcon,
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

/** Atom — single icon from the Zimmermann icon set. Mirrors zimm-icon contract. */
export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];
  // TypeScript cannot index a discriminated union type directly — each branch must be cast
  // individually to access the relevant key without a type error.
  const ariaHidden = (aria as { 'aria-hidden'?: boolean })['aria-hidden'];
  const ariaLabel = (aria as { 'aria-label'?: string })['aria-label'];
  return (
    <Icon
      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};

# STAGE 1 VERIFICATION RESULTS

Baseline control: `npx tsc --noEmit` → **exit 0** before and after all probing.

---

## CLAIM M1 — **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED** (2 of 3 parts; the XOR part is **DISPROVED**)

**Part A — "comment is factually false, compiles clean without the casts": CONFIRMED.**

Copied `zimmIcon/index.tsx`, deleted both casts (`const ariaHidden = aria['aria-hidden'];`), compiled: **exit 0**, zero errors.

The comment's premise is wrong for a specific, demonstrable reason. Forcing tsc to print the rest-element type:

```
error TS2322: Type '{ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: undefined; } |
                    { 'aria-hidden'?: undefined; 'aria-label': string; }' is not assignable to type '0'.
```

Both keys exist in **both** union members (one required, one optional-undefined). Indexing a union by a key present in every member is ordinary, legal TypeScript. There is nothing to work around.

**Part B — "casts widen `'aria-hidden': true` to `boolean`": CONFIRMED.** Mutual-assignability probe, all assertions compiled:

| expression | exact type |
|---|---|
| `aria['aria-hidden']` (no cast) | `true \| undefined` |
| `(aria as {...boolean})['aria-hidden']` | `boolean \| undefined` |
| the two compared | **not equal** |

**Part C — "erase the XOR guarantee of `ZimmIconProps`": DISPROVED.** With the casts *present*, every invalid call site is still rejected:

```
m1c_xor.tsx(9,33):  TS2322  <ZimmIcon aria-hidden aria-label="Close" />  → rejected
m1c_xor.tsx(10,35): TS2322  <ZimmIcon type="close" />                    → rejected
m1c_xor.tsx(11,35): TS2322  <ZimmIcon aria-hidden={false} />             → rejected
m1c_xor.tsx(14,11): TS2322  <ZimmIcon aria-hidden={someBoolean} />       → rejected
```

Both valid branches (`aria-hidden` alone, `aria-label` alone) were accepted. The casts sit *inside the function body* on the already-destructured rest object; the XOR is enforced by the parameter annotation, which a body-local cast cannot reach. The widening is real but **inert** — no invalid value can reach `aria` in the first place, and `boolean | undefined` is still valid for React's `aria-hidden`.

**Minimal fix:** delete lines 140–143's two casts and the two-line comment; index `aria` directly. Minimal because tsc proves no other edit is needed and the external prop contract is provably untouched. The real defect is a false explanatory comment plus a needless loss of literal-type precision — not a safety hole.

---

## CLAIM M2 — **CONFIRMED** (one terminology error in the claim)

**Casts uncommented:** confirmed by inspection; `typescript.md` says reach for `as` only when genuinely overriding inference and "treat that the same as an `any` — comment why", and for null specifically "Prefer a proper null check, an early return".

**The only work they do is null-suppression** — variant (a), casts removed, no guard:

```
m2a_noCasts.tsx(4,16): error TS18047: 'footer' is possibly 'null'.
m2a_noCasts.tsx(5,24): error TS18047: 'footer' is possibly 'null'.
m2a_noCasts.tsx(6,22): error TS18047: 'slot' is possibly 'null'.
```

Three `possibly null` errors and **zero missing-member errors** — which independently proves the `HTMLElement` part is inert.

**`HTMLElement` buys nothing:** `getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect` is declared on `interface Element` (`lib.dom.d.ts:10903`; interface opens at 10701). `footer`/`slot` are used *only* for `.querySelector()` and `.getBoundingClientRect()` — both on `Element`.

Compile matrix: (a) casts removed, no guard → **fails**; (b) `querySelector<HTMLElement>` + guard → **exit 0**; (c) as-is → **exit 0**; (d) plain `Element` + guards → **exit 0**.

**Runtime, executed under jsdom 29.1.1** (`canvasElement: HTMLElement`, confirmed concrete — not `any` — via `WebRenderer` at `storybook/dist/types/index.d.ts:3732`):

```
variant (c) as-is        : TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'querySelector')
variant (b)/(d) guarded  : Error: SubscribePlaceholder: footer[role="contentinfo"] not found
(c) footer ok, slot gone : TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')
(d) footer ok, slot gone : Error: SubscribePlaceholder: [aria-live] slot not found
```

**One correction to the claim:** it calls `Element`→`HTMLElement` a "widening"; it is a *narrowing* (`HTMLElement` is a subtype of `Element`). The substance — that it buys nothing — is correct.

**Also worth calibrating severity:** the as-is version does **not** silently pass. It throws either way, so the story fails. The defect is *diagnostic quality* (an opaque `TypeError` that doesn't name the missing selector), not a false green.

**Minimal fix:** variant (d) — drop both casts, add two `if (!x) throw new Error(...)` guards. Minimal because no generic parameter is needed (`Element` satisfies every use), and it is literally what `typescript.md` prescribes in place of a non-null assertion.

---

## CLAIM S6 — **CONFIRMED** (all three parts, including the important one)

**(1) Read-only access only.** Every use: `legalLinks.map` (index.tsx:435), `navGroups.map` (:454), `group.fields.links.map` (:474). Exhaustive grep for `push|pop|shift|unshift|splice|sort|reverse|fill|copyWithin` and index-assignment across `overrides/` → **NONE FOUND**.

**(2) Exposure is real.** `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is a plain `export const FOOTER_FIXTURE: FooterConfigEntry` module singleton (no `as const`), imported by the **production** `FooterContainer` (index.tsx:557) as well as the stories. A probe performing 6 mutations — `navGroups.push`, index assign, `.sort()`, `.length = 0`, nested `links.push`, `legalLinks?.push` — compiles **today at exit 0**.

**(3) `readonly` breaks nothing — this is the key result.** Validated against a full isolated copy of `overrides/` with its own tsconfig. Control first: untouched copy → **exit 0** (valid baseline). Then with `readonly ... : ReadonlyArray<...>` applied to all three fields:

- Whole tree, no probe → **exit 0**. Nothing breaks: not `FOOTER_FIXTURE`'s object literal, not the component, not the stories, not the placeholder schema.
- With the mutation probe → **all 7 vectors rejected** (`TS2339` push/sort, `TS2542` index signature read-only, `TS2540` length, `TS2540` whole-array reassign).

**Minimal fix:** three lines in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`. Both modifiers pull weight: `ReadonlyArray` blocks push/index/sort/length; the `readonly` property modifier additionally blocks whole-array reassignment (`fields.navGroups = []`). Bonus consistency argument — `footer/index.tsx:356` **already** uses `ReadonlyArray<>` for its own `BottomBarProps.legalLinks`, so this aligns the entry types with the component's existing house style.

## CLAIM S7 — **CONFIRMED**, and it is purely type-level

- `@storybook/react` is in **neither** `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`.
- `npm ls @storybook/react` → `└─┬ @storybook/react-webpack5@10.4.6 └── @storybook/react@10.4.6` — transitive only, exactly as claimed.
- **11** stories import from `@storybook/react-webpack5`; the footer story is the lone outlier (12 story files total).

- **Purely type-level.** It's an `import type`, and with `isolatedModules: true` it is fully erased. Emitted JS: `export const meta = { title: 'X' };` — **0 occurrences** of `@storybook/react`. No runtime footprint whatsoever.

The residual risk is resolution-only: it type-checks today *solely* because npm hoisted `@storybook/react` to top-level `node_modules`. A strict/nested install (pnpm, `--install-strategy=nested`) or a hoisting change would break `tsc` on this one file.

**Minimal fix:** one-word change on line 2.

**No mechanical gate catches M1 or M2.** Type-aware linting *is* configured (`.eslintrc.js:15` → `parserOptions.project`), but `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` reports nothing on either file — by design, since it only flags assertions that don't change the type, and both of these *do* change it (M1 widens, M2 strips null).
